country.name: Algeria
country.tagline: Once the world's biggest wine exporter, now a quiet producer of sun-baked reds from the hills of Oran and Médéa.

stats.note: OIV 2025: 68 kha of vines (table and wine grapes). Wine production around 500,000 hl in the 2010s (Wein-Plus: 492,000 hl in 2012).

country.overview:
Algeria's wine story is one of the most dramatic in the world. Phoenicians, Carthaginians and Romans made wine here, and it faded after the Islamic conquest. Then France arrived in 1830, and when phylloxera destroyed French vineyards from the 1860s, settlers planted the Algerian plains and hills on an enormous scale. Production rose from about 25,000 hectolitres in 1854 to 10 million by 1915; by the late 1930s around 400,000 hectares of vines covered the colony, and by around 1960 output reached some 16 million hectolitres. With Morocco and Tunisia, Algeria then accounted for nearly two thirds of the international wine trade, most of it deep-coloured, high-alcohol red shipped to Sète and blended into the thin wines of the Languedoc.

Independence in 1962 broke the system. The pied-noir growers and the French army, the domestic market, left; France sharply cut its purchases; a Soviet contract from 1969 took 500 million litres a year at low prices; and the state, uneasy about depending on alcohol, encouraged growers to replace vines with cereals and table grapes. Within a few decades the wine vineyard shrank to a small fraction of its colonial peak.

Today the state marketing office ONCV (Office National de Commercialisation des Produits Vitivinicoles) dominates production, alongside a few private companies (Grands Crus de l'Ouest and others). Most vineyards lie in the west around Mascara, Tlemcen, Aïn Témouchent and Sidi Bel Abbès, and in the Médéa and Aïn Bessem hills south of Algiers. Seven quality zones survive from the colonial VDQS: Coteaux de Mascara, Coteaux de Tlemcen, Monts du Tessalah, Dahra, Coteaux du Zaccar, Médéa and Aïn Bessem-Bouira. Wines are sturdy reds from Carignan, Cinsault, Grenache and Alicante Bouschet, rosés, and whites from Clairette and Ugni Blanc.

history.title: The great planting
history.text: As phylloxera ravaged France, settlers planted Algeria; production rose from about 25,000 hl to 10 million hl, helped by winemakers from Baden and the south of France.

history.title: Peak vineyard
history.text: About 400,000 ha of vines covered French Algeria, one of the largest vineyards in the world.

history.title: Sixteen million hectolitres
history.text: Algeria produced around 16 million hl and was the world's largest wine exporter, mostly for blending in southern France.

history.title: Independence and collapse
history.text: The departure of settlers and French cuts in imports, then policy favouring cereals, shrank the vineyard dramatically in the following decades.

country.classification: Seven quality zones (labelled AOG, appellation d'origine garantie) recognised by the ONCV, inherited from French VDQS designations: Coteaux de Mascara, Coteaux de Tlemcen, Monts du Tessalah, Dahra, Coteaux du Zaccar, Médéa and Aïn Bessem-Bouira.
country.climate_soils: Mediterranean climate on the coastal hills and the Tell Atlas, with about 400 mm of rain in the west and 600 mm in the east; vineyards up to about 1,200 metres around Médéa; clay-limestone and sandy soils.

grapes.name: Syrah, Mourvèdre, Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Pinot Noir

further_reading: Wine and Empire: Viticulture in French Algeria (studies by Giulia Meloni and Johan Swinnen)

sources.title: OIV, State of the World Wine Sector in 2025 (Algeria vineyard area)

dz-ain-bessem-bouira.name: Aïn Bessem-Bouira
dz-ain-bessem-bouira.grapes: Carignan, Cinsault, Grenache, Alicante Bouschet, Syrah, Clairette
dz-ain-bessem-bouira.summary: The plateau around Aïn Bessem and Bouira, south-east of Algiers, known for rosés. The plateau lies at 500 to 700 metres between the Djurdjura and the Bibans ranges, with cool nights that suit fresh rosés and light reds from Cinsault and Grenache.

dz-coteaux-de-mascara.name: Coteaux de Mascara
dz-coteaux-de-mascara.grapes: Carignan, Cinsault, Grenache, Alicante Bouschet, Syrah, Clairette
dz-coteaux-de-mascara.summary: The most famous Algerian name, from the hills around Mascara in the west, whose heavy, dark reds were prized for blending in colonial times and are counted among the country's best today.

dz-coteaux-de-tlemcen.name: Coteaux de Tlemcen
dz-coteaux-de-tlemcen.grapes: Carignan, Cinsault, Grenache, Alicante Bouschet, Syrah, Clairette
dz-coteaux-de-tlemcen.summary: Hills around the historic city of Tlemcen near the Moroccan border, at 600 to 900 metres; a source of the ONCV's Cuvée du Président blend. Higher altitude and more rain than the coastal plains give these wines more freshness than most Algerian reds.

dz-coteaux-du-zaccar.name: Coteaux du Zaccar
dz-coteaux-du-zaccar.grapes: Carignan, Cinsault, Grenache, Alicante Bouschet, Syrah, Clairette
dz-coteaux-du-zaccar.summary: The slopes of Mount Zaccar around Miliana, south-west of Algiers. Mount Zaccar rises above the town of Miliana in the Chelif valley, and its slopes give some of the freshest reds and rosés of central Algeria. Like the other zones, it is a colonial VDQS name kept by the ONCV.

dz-dahra.name: Dahra
dz-dahra.grapes: Carignan, Cinsault, Grenache, Alicante Bouschet, Syrah, Clairette
dz-dahra.summary: The coastal Dahra massif between Mostaganem and Ténès, with sea-cooled hillside vineyards; a component of the Cuvée du Président. The Dahra hills, between the Chelif river and the sea, were one of the largest colonial wine areas.

dz-medea.name: Médéa
dz-medea.grapes: Carignan, Cinsault, Grenache, Alicante Bouschet, Syrah, Clairette
dz-medea.summary: High vineyards in the Tell Atlas around Médéa, up to about 1,200 metres, among the coolest in Algeria. Altitude makes Médéa one of the coolest Algerian zones, and its reds are among the most balanced the ONCV bottles. Médéa also supplies the Cuvée du Président blend.

dz-monts-du-tessalah.name: Monts du Tessalah
dz-monts-du-tessalah.grapes: Carignan, Cinsault, Grenache, Alicante Bouschet, Syrah, Clairette
dz-monts-du-tessalah.summary: The Tessala mountains near Sidi Bel Abbès, south of Oran; reds and rosés. The hills sit just west of Sidi Bel Abbès in the heart of the old Oranie wine country, where colonial estates once made bulk wine for blending in southern France. Today the zone produces mainly Carignan and Cinsault reds.

sites.name: Mascara
sites.text: Hill town south-east of Oran, centre of the Coteaux de Mascara zone and of colonial Algeria's most famous wines.

sites.name: Médéa
sites.text: Highland town in the Tell Atlas south of Algiers, centre of the Médéa zone with vineyards up to about 1,200 metres.

sites.name: Tlemcen
sites.text: Historic city of Zayyanid mosques near the Moroccan border at the heart of the Coteaux de Tlemcen, one of Algeria's seven quality zones. Vineyards on the surrounding hills at 600 to 900 metres supply the ONCV's Cuvée du Président blend.

sites.name: Sidi Brahim
sites.text: Village near Sidi Bel Abbès whose name became one of the best-known Algerian wine brands in France.
